The letters are jagged, rough-edged, and brush-painted in faded warm yellow, with torn, claw-like strokes that resemble scratch marks. In the upper-right corner, overlapping the dark forest background and sitting below the title area, there is a small circular price badge reading "10¢" in dark ink on a weathered yellow circle, with a black outline and scratched, printed texture. The central subject is a gigantic moss-covered snail rendered in a painterly, gothic fantasy style. Its body fills most of the middle of the image, with a pale beige-gray, fleshy, wrinkled texture and lichen-like green, brown, and ochre patches spread over its skin. The snail’s head faces downward and slightly left toward a tiny cottage, with two tall, tapered eyestalks rising upward. Its visible eye area is large, glossy, and dark, set within folds of pale tissue, giving it a gentle but eerie expression. Behind and above the head, a massive spiral shell curves diagonally from the lower-left toward the upper-right, partially hidden by tangled branches and moss; the shell has ribbed bands in muted browns, greens, and gray-gold tones. Several soft brown feathers lie around the snail’s shoulders and foreground, adding delicate texture against the rough organic surfaces. The background is a dense, shadowy forest with twisted branches, bare twigs, moss-covered stones, and heavy black-green foliage. The lighting is dim and moody, with subdued forest-dapple effects and deep shadows throughout. In the lower center foreground, a tiny acorn-cap cottage sits on a mossy stump or platform, positioned directly in front of the giant snail from the snail’s point of view. The cottage has a rounded mushroom-like roof, warm brown and ochre wood textures, a small rectangular window with divided panes, and a single glowing warm yellow porch light under the roof. The only bright color in the image is the warm yellow glow emanating from this lantern, which casts a soft halo onto the wooden post, small door area, moss, and nearby objects, creating a cozy contrast against the surrounding darkness. In front of the cottage, on a dark tabletop or stump surface, several found objects are arranged as goblincore junk: a curled downy brown feather on the left, a small spiral snail shell near the center, a rusted teaspoon lying diagonally toward the lower-left, scattered bits of moss and lichen-like growth, and rough organic debris. Additional feathers and a small snail shell appear near the lower-right edge. The entire artwork is framed by a distressed yellow-brown border with scratches, stains, faded edges, creased corners, and darkened corners, making it read as a worn, slightly faded gouache print rather than a clean modern poster. The composition uses a tall portrait layout with the title dominating the top, the colossal snail looming through the center, and the tiny glowing house anchoring the bottom, creating a scale contrast between a cosy miniature dwelling and a towering gentle monster.
